topics.topic: Whether PhotoPlacement.name must match the delivered source file's actual relative name
questions: Must the request-carried `name` be verified to identify the source file whose content is delivered, or is any correctly formed request value authoritative even when it differs from that source's actual relative name?

quotes:
3. One call delivers one photo, named by `name`, a relative path in the form a scan reports, and
   `source_id`. The service keeps no memory of earlier scans: it judges the name and the file when the call
   runs. A named file that passes condition 1 of rule 5 and that A1 orders 1 and 2 do not reject from its
   metadata is opened, and unless the opening decides A1 order 3 or 5, read once; the bytes that were read
   are the bytes judged, hashed and prepared.
judgement.why: State 2 decides that the request-carried name itself selects the source file whose bytes are read, judged, hashed and prepared, so there is no separately selected source path against which that name could differ.
